title: A Small Garden Far from Earth
title_ja: 地球から遠く離れた小さな菜園

source_links.title: NASA Science: The Challenges of Growing Plants in Space

fact_notes: 背景となる考え方は添付の資料で確認。本文と練習問題は新規制作。例示した人物・学校・活動は架空の説明用設定。

sentences.en: When people imagine a long journey through space, they often picture powerful engines and unfamiliar planets.
sentences.ja: 人々が長い宇宙旅行を想像するとき、強力なエンジンや見知らぬ惑星を思い浮かべることがよくあります。

sentences.en: Yet a small garden may be just as interesting to scientists planning how astronauts could live far from Earth.
sentences.ja: しかし地球から遠くで宇宙飛行士が生活する方法を考える科学者にとって、小さな菜園も同じくらい興味深いでしょう。

sentences.en: Fresh vegetables can provide useful nutrients and a welcome change from food stored for long periods.
sentences.ja: 新鮮な野菜は有用な栄養素を提供し、長期間保存された食事からのうれしい変化にもなります。

sentences.en: However, growing plants in space presents challenges that are easy to overlook from a kitchen on Earth.
sentences.ja: しかし宇宙での植物栽培には、地球の台所からは見過ごしやすい課題があります。

sentences.en: A plant needs light, water, nutrients, and a suitable environment regardless of where it grows.
sentences.ja: 植物はどこで育つとしても、光、水、栄養素、適した環境を必要とします。

sentences.en: The difficult task is to provide these conditions inside a limited space without the normal effects of gravity.
sentences.ja: 難しいのは、通常の重力の働きがない限られた空間で、これらの条件を整えることです。

sentences.en: NASA has used plant-growing systems on the International Space Station to investigate these problems.
sentences.ja: NASAは国際宇宙ステーションで植物栽培装置を使い、こうした課題を調べてきました。

sentences.en: In one system called Veggie, plants grow in small containers that hold materials supporting their roots.
sentences.ja: Veggieと呼ばれる装置では、植物は根を支える素材を入れた小さな容器で育ちます。

sentences.en: For example, roots need access to water and air, yet fluids behave differently in microgravity.
sentences.ja: 例えば根には水と空気が必要ですが、微小重力では液体の振る舞いが異なります。

sentences.en: If too much water surrounds the roots, plants may have trouble getting enough oxygen.
sentences.ja: 根の周りに水が多すぎると、植物は十分な酸素を得にくくなるかもしれません。

sentences.en: Special lighting also provides the energy plants need when natural sunlight cannot be used directly.
sentences.ja: 自然光を直接使えない場合、特別な照明が植物に必要なエネルギーを供給します。

sentences.en: These details show why a space garden is an experiment in engineering as well as biology.
sentences.ja: こうした細部は、宇宙の菜園が生物学だけでなく工学の実験でもある理由を示します。

sentences.en: Growing edible plants can create new responsibilities for a crew rather than simply producing extra food.
sentences.ja: 食用植物を育てることは、食料を増やすだけでなく乗組員に新しい責任を生むことがあります。

sentences.en: Astronauts must consider how much time maintenance takes and how carefully the equipment must be monitored.
sentences.ja: 宇宙飛行士は維持管理にかかる時間と、機器に必要な監視の程度を考慮しなければなりません。

sentences.en: In addition, scientists need to check whether the harvested vegetables are safe to eat.
sentences.ja: さらに科学者は収穫した野菜が安全に食べられるかを確かめる必要があります。

sentences.en: A crop that looks healthy may still require testing before it becomes part of a regular menu.
sentences.ja: 健康そうな作物も、日常の献立に加える前に検査が必要かもしれません。

sentences.en: The food produced may supplement stored supplies, but a small garden cannot automatically replace an entire delivery system.
sentences.ja: 育てた食料は備蓄を補えますが、小さな菜園が輸送の仕組み全体を当然のように代替できるわけではありません。

sentences.en: Understanding these limits is essential when people discuss future missions lasting many months.
sentences.ja: 何か月も続く将来の任務を論じるとき、こうした限界を理解することが欠かせません。

sentences.en: Space gardens have another possible benefit that is harder to measure with a simple scale.
sentences.ja: 宇宙の菜園には、単純なはかりでは測りにくいもう一つの利点があり得ます。

sentences.en: Astronauts have described caring for plants as an enjoyable or relaxing activity during their work in orbit.
sentences.ja: 宇宙飛行士は軌道上の作業中、植物の世話が楽しく気分を和らげる活動だと述べてきました。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, such experiences do not prove that every astronaut will react in exactly the same way.
sentences.ja: それでもそうした経験は、すべての飛行士がまったく同じ反応をする証拠ではありません。

sentences.en: Researchers must distinguish personal reports from results that have been tested with suitable methods.
sentences.ja: 研究者は個人の報告と、適切な方法で検証された結果を区別する必要があります。

sentences.en: This distinction matters whenever an exciting scientific idea is discussed in the news.
sentences.ja: この区別は、刺激的な科学の考えがニュースで論じられるとき常に重要です。

sentences.en: A promising possibility becomes reliable knowledge only after careful investigation.
sentences.ja: 有望な可能性は慎重な調査を経て初めて信頼できる知識になります。

sentences.en: Students can use this example to evaluate ambitious plans for living beyond Earth.
sentences.ja: 生徒はこの例を使って、地球外で暮らす意欲的な計画を評価できます。

sentences.en: They might ask which problems are already being studied and which solutions remain uncertain.
sentences.ja: すでに研究中の問題と、まだ不確かな解決策を尋ねられます。

sentences.en: Therefore, the question is not simply whether plants can grow in space but how useful and dependable the system could become.
sentences.ja: したがって問いは宇宙で植物が育つかだけでなく、装置がどれほど役立ち信頼できるかです。

sentences.en: A successful mission depends on many connected technologies, not on one impressive experiment alone.
sentences.ja: 成功する任務は一つの印象的な実験だけでなく、多くのつながった技術に依存します。

sentences.en: The little garden reveals a larger lesson: exploring new worlds requires practical thinking as well as bold imagination.
sentences.ja: 小さな菜園は、新たな世界の探査には大胆な想像力だけでなく実際的な思考も必要だと教えます。

questions.prompt: What is the central argument of the passage?
options: Plants will replace every spacecraft system.
Space gardening is already free of technical problems.
Growing plants in space involves practical, scientific, and human challenges.
Space research should focus only on engines.
questions.explanation_ja: 植物栽培の技術的・科学的・人的課題を総合的に考えることが中心です。

questions.prompt: Why are fresh vegetables valuable on long space journeys?
options: They provide nutrients and variety in food.
They remove the need for oxygen.
They can be stored without any care.
questions.explanation_ja: 栄養と食事の変化をもたらすことが説明されています。

questions.prompt: Why is gravity important to the discussion of roots?
options: Gravity makes all plants grow instantly.
Water and air behave differently when gravity is very weak.
Space gardens receive too much sunlight.
questions.explanation_ja: 水・空気の分布が地上と異なるためです。

questions.prompt: What might happen if roots receive too much water?
options: The plants may struggle to get oxygen.
questions.explanation_ja: 根が十分な酸素を得にくくなります。

questions.prompt: What does the NASA system Veggie help scientists study?
options: The history of cooking on Earth.
questions.explanation_ja: 宇宙の条件下での植物栽培を研究する装置です。

questions.prompt: Why does a space crop need safety testing?
options: It must be checked before being used as regular food.
All crops grow only in darkness.
questions.explanation_ja: 見た目だけで安全性を判断できないためです。
supplementは不足分を補うという意味です。

questions.prompt: What personal experience did some astronauts report?
options: They felt every plant was harmful.
They could not understand the experiment.
They found caring for plants enjoyable or relaxing.
questions.explanation_ja: 植物の世話を楽しい・安らぐ活動と述べた報告があります。

questions.prompt: Why distinguish personal reports from tested findings?
options: Personal experiences always provide exact proof.
An interesting report is not automatically a general scientific result.
Every astronaut has the same feelings.
questions.explanation_ja: 個別経験を一般化された科学的結果と混同しないためです。

questions.prompt: Why does the final sentence mention imagination and practical thinking?
options: To argue that useful exploration requires both creativity and careful planning.
To suggest space exploration should stop.
To say gardening is the only useful science.
To claim experiments no longer matter.
questions.explanation_ja: 想像力と現実的な検討の両立を結論にします。
